ir1_coup.topic: Iran's recognition of Israel (1950) and the 1953 coup

claims.text: Iran voted against the UN partition plan in 1947
On 6 March 1950, during a Majlis recess, the Iranian government recognised Israel de facto 'without formal announcement'; Iran never extended de jure recognition
On 7 July 1951, shortly after Mosaddegh took power, Iran closed its Jerusalem consulate citing 'financial difficulties' but did not revoke de facto recognition
Iran was the second Muslim-majority country after Turkey to recognise Israel; Israel kept a de facto embassy in Tehran
Mosaddegh became prime minister 29 April 1951 and nationalised the British-owned oil industry two days later; Britain imposed sanctions and covert operations

US and British officials agreed plan AJAX on 3 February 1953, with final approval 25 June 1953; first attempt c.15 August failed; shah fled to Baghdad then Rome; on 19 August crowds paid by the CIA and army units overthrew Mosaddegh; Zahedi became PM; Mosaddegh convicted of treason

CIA internal history 'The Battle for Iran', released via FOIA and published by the National Security Archive in August 2013: 'The military coup that overthrew Mossadegh and his National Front Cabinet was carried out under CIA direction'
Takeyh argues the second coup was 'very much an Iranian initiative' and that 'Iranian royalists had more at stake and more to lose than the Americans'

Brew surveys the historiography: Gasiorowski (communism), Abrahamian (oil), revisionists Bayandor and Takeyh downplay foreign role; Azimi responds to revisionists; Brew argues a 'collapse narrative' drove the decision

ir1_periphery.topic: Periphery doctrine, SAVAK-Mossad, trade, arms, Project Flower, 1973

claims.text: In the late 1950s Israel sought friendship with 'the neighbors of the neighbors' (periphery policy), producing an informal alliance with Iran

Trident (Israel, Iran, Turkey) formed through meetings in Europe, Ankara and Tehran 1956-58; heads of intelligence services set up cooperative ventures against Nasserist and Soviet influence; 'a lopsided intelligence alliance'; Israel 'provided far better information and more intelligence know-how than it received'
In a 1975 interview the Shah acknowledged military and intelligence ties with Israel, justified by Arab hostility in Nasser's era, adding 'the situation has changed'
In September 1957 SAVAK chief Teymur Bakhtiar offered intelligence exchange to Israel's ambassador in Paris; Israel welcomed it
Abrahamian: Mossad, the CIA and the FBI helped establish SAVAK in 1957; Milani: Mossad and the CIA assisted its creation
Iraqi Zionist underground smuggled Jews to Iran at about 1,000 a month by 1949, then on to Israel; airlift 1951-52 of 120,000-130,000 Iraqi Jews via Iran and Cyprus
Iran became a transit point for Iraqi Jews

Israeli exports to Iran rose from $22.3m (1970) to $92.4m (1975) and $103.2m (1977); imports (non-oil) from $1.3m (1967) to $5.8m (1977), per Israeli official statistics; Israel trained Iranian officers; Israeli school in Tehran
More than 500 Israeli families lived in Iran before the revolution (Israeli FM archives); Arafat received the keys to the former Israeli mission on 19 February 1979
On 24 July 1960 the Shah publicly reaffirmed recognition of Israel; Nasser broke relations with Iran; distancing from Israel was a tool for reconciling with Arab states

Project Flower: one of six oil-for-arms contracts signed April 1977; Toufanian met Dayan and Weizman in Israel 18 July 1977; Iran paid $280m in oil as down payment in 1978; assembly plant near Sirjan, test range near Rafsanjan; ended with the revolution in 1979; Bergman reports Israel planned to give obsolete technology

NYT (reported via JTA, April 1986): documents left by Israeli diplomats in Tehran show the missile project 'Flower'; 'the Israelis told the Iranians that the missiles could be fitted with nuclear warheads'; officials interviewed did not deny authenticity
Iran did not join the 1973 Arab (OAPEC) embargo and increased production; the Shah pushed for higher prices
Alpher writes that in 1973 the Shah 'joined the Arab-led oil embargo' and cut Iranian oil shipments to Israel

On 6 October 1973 Egypt's navy blocked Bab al-Mandeb, cutting Israel off from its main supply, Iran; in 1967 about 90% of Israel's oil imports came from Iran through Tiran; by the mid-1970s Sinai wells supplied over half of Israel's consumption

During the 1973 war the Shah sent a congratulatory telegram to Sadat and approved a one-time Soviet overflight of six planes to Baghdad, revoking a later 32-plane permission (Mirfendereski recollection)

claims.text: EAPC agreement signed February 1968; Israel and Iran equal partners; Iranian side NIOC through shell companies (Trans-Asiatic Oil, Panama; APC Holdings, Canada); 254 km 42-inch line Eilat-Ashkelon; most oil re-exported to Europe; peak 10 million tons in 1970; 49-year franchise expired 2017
Golda Meir proposed the joint venture during a secret visit to Tehran in July 1965; Trans-Asiatic incorporated in Switzerland 1968; pipeline operating 1969; Deutsche Bank financing
Pipeline initially carried over ten million tons a year, more than Israel's annual consumption

Secrecy: 17 July 1968 decree made pipeline information a state secret; leaking classified EAPC information punishable by 15 years to life (2017); a 2024 amendment narrowed the order slightly; State Comptroller January 2025 report cited failures
Iran's claim filed 1994: payment for last oil shipments before the revolution and share of joint assets; Israel counterclaimed for breach of supply contract; arbitration in Switzerland

May 2015: arbitral award ordered payment of about $1.1bn to Iran (reported as $1.2bn plus $362m interest in some accounts); 27 June 2016 Swiss Federal Tribunal rejected Israel's appeal, awarded CHF 450,000 costs
Israel's Finance Ministry: 'Under the laws of trade we cannot transfer funds to an enemy country'; Israel designated Iran an enemy state in 2011; Israel argues EAPC had no value in 1979
In January 2018 both sides' representatives wrote they were willing to talk to settle; a 2019 Geneva hearing apparently never took place; Finance Ministry and PMO declined comment (December 2024)
April 2024: Israeli officials reportedly discussed seizing an EAPC fund (over $1bn, 50% of profits set aside) owed to Iran to offset costs of Iran's 13 April attack
After the revolution Iran embargoed oil to Israel; Israel used spot markets and clandestine trade through the pipeline organised by Marc Rich
